html:
Erdene Zuu, at Kharkhorin in central Mongolia, is the oldest surviving Buddhist monastery in the country, founded in 1585 by Abtai Sain Khan of the Khalkha Mongols. It was built partly with stone from the ruins of Karakorum, the old capital of the Mongol Empire, which stood beside it.

Abtai had taken up the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism, newly brought to the Mongols when Altan Khan gave the title of Dalai Lama to its leader in 1578. Erdene Zuu helped spread the faith among the Khalkha. Its square compound is ringed by a wall topped with about a hundred white stupas, with temples in Tibetan and Chinese styles inside.

At its height it had dozens of temples and hundreds of monks. In the late 1930s the communist government destroyed most of Mongolia's monasteries; here only a few temples and the wall survived, kept as a museum. Worship resumed after 1990, and the site is part of the Orkhon Valley World Heritage Site.
